title: Joy Comes with the Morning
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: For anyone in a long dry season: the Lord is near, he is for you, and his favor is for a lifetime. Look to the cross and keep going.
exhortation: This morning I want to speak to those of us who feel like we've been in a long dry season. There have been times when we felt the nearness of the Lord and had sweet fellowship with him, and now it isn't easy to feel what we felt before. It can be confusing. I've felt that myself: "Lord, why is it so hard? It used to be so easy."

This psalm reminds me that the Lord is for us and with us through it all. It brings to mind Hebrews, where it says the Lord disciplines those he loves. There are seasons when he is teaching us through discipline, and we need to listen and trust his faithfulness and love as we go through them. He is not far away. He is near.

I don't always know why. There are times of discipline. There are times when my heart is cold because I've sown seeds of coldness and dryness through my own decisions. And there are times it isn't easily explained. So we need to go back to the cross, back to his heart. His heart is for us. "His anger is but for a moment, and his favor is for a lifetime." He isn't annoyed or frustrated with us. He is for us in the discipline as much as in the sweet times.

Look at what he did: he came, lived and died so that we might have fellowship with him. On this side of heaven, things can be hard, and everything we do is tainted with sin, so it can be confusing. But through Scripture and through the cross, we know he is for us and working in our lives. Don't let go of that truth. Keep reading the word, keep going to church and fellowshipping, and keep praying, because he is near, he is for us, and he is doing everything for our good.
prayer: Lord, you are the God who breathes life into the valley of dry bones. You make life where there is none. Some of us are in a dry season, for whatever reason. May we not lose hope. May we fix our eyes on you, Jesus, the founder and perfecter of our faith, who endured the cross. You are still with us, whatever our feelings tell us.

So we put our trust in you completely, and we ask for seasons of great renewal, when we feel your nearness again, and boldness for mission, encouragement, strength and confidence come, so that we run this race well. Help us do it, Lord. In Jesus' name, amen.
